thread:
pm_jordan: Thanks for coming to today's all-hands. Leaving a short follow-up thread to capture leadership Q&A follow-ups. Two quick asks to start: 1) what does 'winning' look like in ~18 months, and 2) how should teams prioritize infra vs product bets? I'll collect notes here.

ceo_anna: Good thread — short answer: winning = 3 things. 1) Redwood is the default for production inference across hosted/dedicated/private, 2) customers choose us because inference is both predictable and cheaper than the pain of self-hosting, 3) teams can roll out and operate LLM features without building infra. We should bias first to reliability and demonstrable economics.

eng_lead_maya: When you say "cheaper" — do you mean $/token at scale or total operational TCO vs self-hosting? This affects infra roadmaps and what we benchmark.

cto_lee: Both. Sales needs TCO comparisons; infra/product teams need $/k token at target percentiles. Practically we improve both by focusing on batching, KV cache hit rates, and model + quantization profiles.

sales_sam: For enterprise RFPs customers ask about vendor lock-in and comparison to hyperscalers + OSS stacks. Can we get a short positioning doc?

ceo_anna: Yes. We'll produce a 1-pager for RFPs. Messaging: unified runtime + predictable economics + cross-environment portability. Emphasize exportable model versions and configs so customers aren't locked in.

ops_rita: Private deployment roadmap question: which is higher priority — VPC GA or an on-prem appliance? We have pilot deals asking for offline appliance.

design_kai: Product/Design question: should we invest more in console UX for rollouts and visibility, or surface deeper runtime controls via API for platform teams?

cto_lee: Both matter. Early wins: invest in console UX for rollouts to reduce day-1 friction. Medium term: expose runtime knobs via API for platform teams that need programmatic control.

eng_lead_maya: For infra planning we also need perf SLO targets by model class. Suggest starting list:
```
short (<=128 tokens): p95 < 100ms, p99 < 250ms
medium (129-1024): p95 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms
long (>1024): p95 < 400ms, p99 < 900ms
```
We can iterate but want baseline to size capacity.

research_asha: On competitors — are we differentiating mainly by serving runtime (tech) or by product/ops experience? That will decide how we prioritize benchmarks and benchmark stories.

ceo_anna: The differentiation is the combination: tech (serving runtime) is our barrier; product and ops is how we win deals. Benchmarks should highlight tail latency, cost per effective token, and reliability under mixed workloads.

allhands_bot: Recording uploaded: https://redwood.internal/all-hands/1954321000 (slides attached in thread).

pm_jordan: Action items from this thread: (a) @cto_lee + @eng_lead_maya draft perf SLOs (b) @sales_sam + @ceo_anna draft the RFP 1-pager (c) @ops_rita prioritize private pilots and clarify appliance vs VPC tradeoffs. I'll gather drafts by EOD Friday and synthesize into a short one-pager.

eng_lead_maya: :thumbsup: starting a doc in the infra repo now, will ping infra team for metrics.

sales_sam: If anyone can share anonymized customer TCO numbers or RFP asks please drop them here or DM — would help shape the 1-pager.

ceo_anna: Thanks everyone. Quick sync next Tue 10am to finalize messaging — 1 slide each.

pm_jordan: I'll create the calendar invite and a summary doc in the repo. Thanks all for rapid responses.
